title: Fixings, support and disassembly
intro: Support design starts with load paths, the supporting substrate and access for service. Distinguish bearing support from restraint without turning a sketch into a universal fixing prescription.
goals: Trace load paths and support type
Identify the substrate and fixing system

sections.title: Trace load paths and support type
sections.text: A floor-standing unit transfers weight through its parts and base or legs to the floor. A wall-hung unit transfers it through carcass connections and suspension to the wall. These paths define the review scope, not adequacy. Distinguish vertical weight from a user pull at a handle and identify bearing and restraint points for each use case.
sections.caption: Floor-bearing and wall-hung load paths differ.

sections.title: Identify the substrate and fixing system
sections.text: Paint or tile does not identify the load-bearing substrate. Document its construction, condition and concealed services using site information. The detail must show carcass, support member, carcass-to-support connection and support-to-substrate connection. Fixing type, number, size and location require system-specific technical review; this lesson provides planning, not drilling instructions.
sections.caption: Review both carcass-to-support and support-to-substrate connections.

sections.title: Plan service access before closure
sections.text: A cover may hide adjustment or fixing points; define access without destroying finishes. Draw cover removal and service sequence, identifying any temporary support needed in a competent specialist’s plan. Do not treat a load-carrying connection as a freely removable cover. Retain system references, fixing locations and inspection records with approved maintenance instructions.
sections.caption: Service access must preserve the required support plan.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: Option A shows a screw into a finish without identifying its substrate. B shows carcass, support, substrate and both connections, flagging load and substrate information for review. B is a more complete review package because it exposes the load path and unknowns; it is not installation approval.
example.decision: Decision: develop B as a review package; do not issue it for installation before technical verification.

quiz.question: What is missing when the sketch shows a fixing only into the finish?
quiz.explanation: The finish does not identify the supporting substrate or complete connection chain.

assignment.prompt: Submit floor-standing/wall-hung load paths, a support detail and a substrate/service review list.

faq.question: Can any connector be removed for access?
faq.answer: No. Review its load-carrying role and specialist support/disassembly plan first.
